{{nihongo|'''Sunomata Shrine'''|墨俣神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Sunomata, Gifu|Q7640962|qid=Q7640962}}, {{ill|Ōgaki|Q384926|qid=Q384926}}, {{ill|Gifu Prefecture|Q131277|qid=Q131277}}. It is a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shikinaisha}}. It is north of {{ill|Ogaki Municipal Sunomata Elementary School|Q11433783|qid=Q11433783}}. {{nihongo|'''Sunomata Shrine'''|墨俣神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Mino Province]].

== Enshrined deity ==
* Sunomata Ōkami<ref name="岐阜県神社庁">[https://www.gifu-jinjacho.jp/syosai.php?shrno=2 Sunomata Shrine] Gifu Prefectural Shrine Association</ref>

== History ==
== Founding ==
Founding period is unknown<ref name="墨俣町1956p414">Sunomata Town History Compilation Committee, 'History of Sunomata Town,' Sunomata Town, 1956, pp.414-416</ref>. In the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}, the enshrined deity is also "Sunomata Ōkami," but which deity this refers to is unclear. In the 'Mino no Kuni Jinmyōchō,' said to have been compiled in Tenkei/Tentoku years (938-961), it appears as "Junior Fifth Rank Lower, Sunomata Myōjin"<ref name="墨俣町1956p414"/>.

Originally it was south of the Sunomata ferry crossing<ref name="墨俣町1956p414"/>. In Kyōhō 2 (1717), investigation by {{ill|Nangū Taisha|Q704967|qid=Q704967}} identified it with Sunomata Shrine in the Engishiki register<ref name="墨俣町1956p414"/>.

== Modern and contemporary ==
In 1873 (Meiji 6), it was ranked as gōsha under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}<ref name="墨俣町1956p414"/>.

In the {{ill|Meiji era|lt=Meiji period|qid=Q3125096}}, river improvement work on the {{ill|Sai River (Gifu)|Q7399814|qid=Q7399814|lt=Saigawa}} began to reduce flood damage, and in 1935 (Shōwa 10) the shrine moved to its present location<ref name="すのまた旅">[https://gifuogaki.com/sunomata-history/ History] Sunomata Travel</ref>.

== Precinct ==
[[File:Sunomata-jinja Ogaki 2025-12 ac (3).jpg|thumb|Base of all-night lantern]]
* Shrine buildings
* Akiba Shrine - precinct shrine; history unclear<ref name="墨俣町1956p414"/>.
* Mikuwa Shrine - precinct shrine; history unclear<ref name="墨俣町1956p414"/>.
* Shinmei Shrine - precinct shrine. On March 27, 1907 (Meiji 40), designated a {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=shrine receiving offerings of sacred food and silk}}<ref name="墨俣町1956p414"/>.
* Base of all-night lantern - base section of a {{ill|Waniguchi|ja|鰐口|qid=Q11674315|lt=all-night lantern}} said to have stood at Sunomata ferry was placed in the precincts<ref>Seiichi Yoneyama, 'Exploring Sunomata History,' Seiichi Yoneyama, 1992, p.51</ref>. Commonly called "Gotōsan." The lantern was completed around Bunka 12 (1815), but on October 28, 1891 (Meiji 24), the {{ill|1891 Mino–Owari earthquake|Q2351002|qid=Q2351002}} broke its firebox and shaft. It was first moved beside the great torii of Sunomata Shrine, and in 1933 (Shōwa 8), moved again to the current location with shrine relocation.

== Access ==
*5 minutes on foot from {{ill|Meihan Kintetsu Bus|Q11415818|qid=Q11415818}} Gikaki Line "Sunomata" stop
**From {{ill|Ōgaki Station bus terminal|Q11433817|qid=Q11433817}} (south of {{ill|Ōgaki Station|Q871579|qid=Q871579}}), platform 2, bound for "{{ill|Gifu Shotoku Gakuen University|Q5560125|qid=Q5560125}}" / "South Gifu Distribution Center"
*5 minutes on foot from {{ill|Gifu Bus|Q5560101|qid=Q5560101|lt=Gifu Bus}} Obusa-Sunomata Line "Sunomata" stop
**From {{ill|JR Gifu Station Bus Terminal|Q11226229|qid=Q11226229}} (north of {{ill|Gifu Station|Q1144885|qid=Q1144885}}), platform 6, bound for "W65 Sunomata"
**From {{ill|Meitetsu Gifu stop|Q11415771|qid=Q11415771}} (west of {{ill|Meitetsu Gifu Station|Q1109902|qid=Q1109902}}), platform 1, bound for "W65 Sunomata"
